best_idea: Give every client request a class with a per-tick cap, charge a rejected request to its own class, and validate each op against the server's current scene state before any effect.
decision_why: The idea (per-tick intake cap by class plus server-side op validation) fits our one-engine, server-verified-kill rulings. The donor's bucket bug (rejected user input charged to the client budget) and its unmeasured numbers are fixed in the sketch; the 52-tile window becomes zone data and the hop timer is skipped while we run one runtime.
acceptance: A server test sends 50 fight-action messages in one tick: only 5 are handled, the rest wait for the next tick, a rejected action uses one of the 5 slots, and an action on a tile outside the fighter's scene window leaves the fighter's state unchanged.
